coaching.headline: A mixed sweep: carry, jungle and support lanes won clean, the offlane lost to Greystone all game — and still only six of nine won fights got converted.
coaching.team: Three lanes read favored (carry, jungle, support), and only the offlane, Grux against Greystone, ran unfavored the whole game. Two Fangtooths, at minute six and minute seventeen, fell with all five of us alive and unchallenged — a choice, not a bad trade, twice in a game we still won big. From there the team simply out-fought the opponent: nine fights won to their one, river control eighteen to six, and objective damage 36,080 to 16,798. Six of the nine won fights got converted into a tower or objective; three were left on the board. Towers closed it out ten to two. Next game: send a body to contest the free Fangtooth instead of letting it walk.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Nine fights won to their one, plus river control eighteen to six, built the lead early. The risk was two uncontested Fangtooths, at minute six and seventeen, that never got punished only because everything else ran this lopsided.
coaching.whatWorked: The fight conversion: nine fights won to their one, six of them cashed into a tower or objective.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: GRIM.exe was the closer: sixteen kills to two deaths, repeatedly finishing Sparrow and Yin in the fights that flipped towers, and 37,098 damage to heroes led the team. Getting caught alone by Sparrow at 11.9 continues a habit flagged in two of his last three films — this time it cost nothing.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel did the frontline job: 47,056 mitigated, the team's best, 54% kill participation and a team-high 17 assists — the carry never died before minute ten. The crack was getting caught alone by Yin at 6.2, a habit flagged in his last three films, with only 4 wards to Mourn's 6.
perPlayer.dd4f2929-42c2-4590-997b-65050da475c3: Serath won the jungle matchup early, with first blood on Mourn at 3.5 and two more kills on Yin before minute ten, but faded late — going down five times, the most on the winning side, including a solo catch by Sparrow at 12.6. No armor went into a four-fifths-physical enemy comp.
perPlayer.d3c78837-0a96-4b88-a128-e6c81e39b905: Grux lost the lane matchup to Greystone the whole game, but still finished six kills to three deaths by winning teamfights instead. Both of his other deaths were costly: caught alone at 4.7, giving up Fangtooth, and again at 18.2, handing over the Outer Tower.
perPlayer.f2c3109e-dd1b-4540-b48d-abcd086cd6d1: Valmont dominated mid: seven kills for two deaths, four of them on Revenant alone, and 33,519 damage to heroes, second only to GRIM.exe. Both deaths came early to the enemy jungle: Yin caught him at 8.5 and again at 11.3, but from there he took over the matchup completely.

20.7.call: The fight at 20.7 was won four kills to one, but our Inner Tower still fell — the bodies won, the objective lost.

22.1.call: Down a body after Serath went down 34 seconds earlier, the 22.1 fight was won five-to-one and closed Primal Fangtooth anyway — entering 4v5 was still the riskier call, even though it paid off.

24.3.call: The 24.3 fight was won six kills to one at their Inner Tower, but Serath (alive, winning lane) and Valmont (alive) both sat it out — bring the full five next time, even to a fight this lopsided.

ranking.grade: GRIM.exe was best on the roster: sixteen kills, two deaths, 37,098 damage to heroes.
Valmont was second: seven kills, two deaths, and four of those kills alone on Revenant.
Steel was third: 47,056 damage mitigated and a team-high 17 assists held the front line.
Grux was fourth: lost the offlane matchup all game; two solo catches cost Fangtooth and a tower.
Serath was fifth: five deaths, the most on the team, and no armor into a four-fifths-physical comp.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: GRIM.exe skipped the community's higher-winrate Dust Devil path (Lightning Hawk, Plasma Blade, Dust Devil at 55.4%) for Sky Splitter's percent-health shred against Greystone's tankiness — a situational call the winrate data doesn't actually back.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The engine's pick for GRIM.exe is Demiurge, which fits his sustained basic-attack output, trading away the extra tankiness a defensive option like Krix would offer against Yin's dives.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Steel skipped Gaia Greaves' physical armor for Flux Matrix's magical armor and Prophecy's magic damage, against a comp that was four-fifths physical — the wrong resistance to stack, even though 47,056 mitigated damage got away with it.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Our engine doesn't model support Eternals like Exarch, Weald or Marrow, so there's no numeric read for Steel here — the field mostly runs a peel-first major on frontline supports like this.

dd4f2929-42c2-4590-997b-65050da475c3.build: Serath skipped the winning core (Sky Splitter, Storm Breaker, Spectra) entirely for a lethality path (Manta Scythe, Viper, Deathstalker), with no armor into a comp that was four-fifths physical, and five deaths, some to that same physical damage, followed.
dd4f2929-42c2-4590-997b-65050da475c3.eternal: The engine's pick for Serath is also Demiurge, boosting the burst inside her dive combo, at the cost of the extra survivability a tankier option would give for repeated dives into a frontline like Greystone's.

d3c78837-0a96-4b88-a128-e6c81e39b905.build: Grux swapped the meta Rapture for Tainted Blade, trading self-sustain for the team's only anti-heal item — the right answer to Mourn's healing, since just one of five of us carried any.
d3c78837-0a96-4b88-a128-e6c81e39b905.eternal: The engine's Demiurge pick for Grux boosts his 20-second-fight burst, at the cost of the raw survivability a tankier alternative would add against a losing matchup like this one.

f2c3109e-dd1b-4540-b48d-abcd086cd6d1.build: There's no tracked meta build for valmont this patch, so there's no baseline to weigh his Orb of Enlightenment, Magnify, Overseer and Caustica against — on the numbers alone, 33,519 damage to heroes and seven kills, it did the job.
f2c3109e-dd1b-4540-b48d-abcd086cd6d1.eternal: No eternal loadout is tracked for valmont in our engine either, so there's no fit-read to give here beyond the numbers he put up.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 1 item of it.
Enemy is 4/5 physical — a single armor item blunts most of their damage; itemize armor on anyone diveable.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Energy Shield block → Displacement Blast → Assault Mode → GTFO lockon ult
ourKits.winCondition: out-trade with Pulsefire and the spell-shield, finish with GTFO
ourKits.playWith: peel so he can free-cast in Assault Mode
ourKits.playAgainst: bait Energy Shield, then commit; dodge GTFO's slow channel

ourKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
ourKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
ourKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
ourKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

ourKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
ourKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
ourKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
ourKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Abduct pull → Contagion ally-heal bugs → Beguile damage-reduction → Eclipse vision-denial ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and sustain the team through the brawl
enemyKits.playWith: burst that punishes his pulled target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect the long Abduct channel/range; anti-heal blunts Contagion

enemyKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
enemyKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak

enemyKits.combo: Lash Kick gap-close+slow → Windburn %hp basics → Backlash push, Quelling Gale to disengage
enemyKits.passive: Rising Storm stacks grant attack speed
enemyKits.playWith: a team that lets her side-lane and pick
enemyKits.playAgainst: she wants 1v1s — group and burst her; Quelling Gale only stops projectiles

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
